components.note: 走 (walk, run) — movement: 起, 超, 趣, 赶; 越 is to cross over, to exceed.
戉 (yuè) sounds exactly like 越.
南 (nán) — south; as a part it sounds out 楠 nán and 喃 nán.

example.hanzi: 越南的咖啡很有名。
example.pinyin: Yuènán de kāfēi hěn yǒumíng.
example.english: Vietnam's coffee is very famous.
example.fact: Vietnam is the world's second-largest coffee producer after Brazil, and its output is dominated by robusta beans rather than the arabica more common elsewhere. Most of this coffee is grown in the Central Highlands region around Dak Lak province, where volcanic soil and a distinct dry season create ideal growing conditions. The country's coffee exports only took off after economic reforms in the late 1980s, transforming it from a minor producer into a global powerhouse within a couple of decades.

examples.hanzi: 我明年想去越南旅游,听说那里的风景很美。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngnián xiǎng qù Yuènán lǚyóu, tīngshuō nàlǐ de fēngjǐng hěn měi.
examples.english: I want to travel to Vietnam next year; I hear the scenery there is beautiful.

examples.hanzi: 我最喜欢吃越南河粉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan chī Yuènán héfěn.
examples.english: My favorite food is Vietnamese pho.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
见 (see) — seeing and looking, as in 现, 觉, 看: 视 is to look.
礻 here is 示 (shì), the altar radical in 礼 and 神: in 视 it is the exact sound clue.

example.hanzi: 他完全无视了老师的警告。
example.pinyin: Tā wánquán wúshì le lǎoshī de jǐnggào.
example.english: He completely ignored the teacher's warning.
example.fact: The RMS Titanic received at least six iceberg warnings by wireless on the day it sank in April 1912, but several were never relayed to the officers on the bridge. The ship continued at near-full speed through the night despite the reports. Historians still debate how differently the crew might have acted had every warning reached the right hands in time.

examples.hanzi: 司机无视红灯,直接开了过去。
examples.pinyin: Sījī wúshì hóngdēng, zhíjiē kāiguòqù le.
examples.english: The driver ignored the red light and drove straight through.

examples.hanzi: 你不能无视别人的感受。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bù néng wúshì biéren de gǎnshòu.
examples.english: You can't disregard other people's feelings.

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — marks birds, as in 鸡 chicken, 鹅 goose; 鹰 is the eagle or hawk.

example.hanzi: 一只鹰在天空中飞。
example.pinyin: Yì zhī yīng zài tiānkōng zhōng fēi.
example.english: An eagle is flying in the sky.
example.fact: 鹰 is counted with 只. 老鹰 is the everyday word, and 老鹰捉小鸡 ("the eagle catches the chicks") is a popular children's game. 雄鹰 means a mighty eagle, and 鹰派 is a hawk in politics.

examples.hanzi: 那只老鹰正在山顶盘旋。
examples.pinyin: Nà zhī lǎoyīng zhèngzài shāndǐng pánxuán.
examples.english: That eagle is circling above the mountaintop.

examples.hanzi: 鹰的眼睛非常锐利。
examples.pinyin: Yīng de yǎnjing fēicháng ruìlì.
examples.english: An eagle's eyes are extremely sharp.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫; 咒 is a curse spoken aloud.

example.hanzi: 魔法师念了一句咒语。
example.pinyin: Mófǎshī niàn le yí jù zhòuyǔ.
example.english: The magician recited a spell.
example.fact: 咒 is a spell or curse: 咒语, 念咒 (to chant a spell), 诅咒 (to curse). 紧箍咒, the headband spell that controls the Monkey King in Journey to the West, is now a metaphor for a rule that keeps you in check.

examples.hanzi: 你别咒我，我会好好的。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié zhòu wǒ, wǒ huì hǎohāo de.
examples.english: Don't curse me, I will be just fine.

examples.hanzi: 故事里的巫婆给王子下了咒。
examples.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ de wūpó gěi wángzǐ xià le zhòu.
examples.english: In the story the witch put a curse on the prince.

meanings: to take a turn for the better

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
车 (cart) — 车 is a cart or vehicle, as in 轮, 输, 车; 转 is turning of wheels.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 转 is zhuǎn; 专 also sounds out 传 chuán and 砖 zhuān.

example.hanzi: 经过治疗,他的病情逐渐好转。
example.pinyin: Jīngguò zhìliáo, tā de bìngqíng zhújiàn hǎozhuǎn.
example.english: After treatment, his condition gradually improved.
example.fact: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin somewhat by accident in 1928, after noticing that mold had killed the bacteria in a contaminated petri dish. It took over a decade, and the urgent needs of World War II, before scientists worked out how to mass-produce it. Once available, penicillin turned once-fatal bacterial infections into conditions from which patients could reliably recover.

examples.hanzi: 吃了药以后,我感冒慢慢好转了。
examples.pinyin: Chīle yào yǐhòu, wǒ gǎnmào mànmàn hǎozhuǎn le.
examples.english: After taking the medicine, my cold gradually got better.

examples.hanzi: 天气明天会好转,不用太担心。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì míngtiān huì hǎozhuǎn, bú yòng tài dānxīn.
examples.english: The weather will improve tomorrow, so don't worry too much.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.

example.hanzi: 这双鞋的大小正合适。
example.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié de dàxiǎo zhèng héshì.
example.english: The size of these shoes fits just right.
example.fact: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived, reaching lengths of up to 30 meters and weights of nearly 200 tons. Its heart alone can weigh as much as a small car, and its calls can be louder than a jet engine. Even the largest dinosaurs, like Argentinosaurus, likely fell short of the blue whale in overall mass.

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服大小不合适,我想换一件。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu dàxiǎo bù héshì, wǒ xiǎng huàn yí jiàn.
examples.english: This garment isn't the right size, so I'd like to exchange it.

examples.hanzi: 家里大小事情都是妈妈做主。
examples.pinyin: Jiālǐ dàxiǎo shìqing dōu shì māma zuòzhǔ.
examples.english: Mom makes the decisions on all matters in the family, big and small.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — clothes and wear: 衬, 被, 袋; 装 is dress, then to pretend or to load.
壮 (zhuàng) is a near sound match for zhuāng; also in 状 zhuàng and 妆 zhuāng.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.

example.hanzi: 她装作没看见我。
example.pinyin: Tā zhuāngzuò méi kànjiàn wǒ.
example.english: She pretended not to see me.
example.fact: Opossums really do "play dead" when threatened, a behavior called thanatosis. It is an involuntary, catatonic response rather than a conscious act — the animal's body goes limp, its breathing slows, and it can even release a foul odor to complete the illusion of a rotting carcass. The state can last anywhere from minutes to hours, and the opossum has no control over when it ends.

examples.hanzi: 他明明很难过,却装作没事的样子。
examples.pinyin: Tā míngmíng hěn nánguò, què zhuāngzuò méishì de yàngzi.
examples.english: He was clearly sad but pretended nothing was wrong.

examples.hanzi: 别装作不懂,我知道你明白。
examples.pinyin: Bié zhuāngzuò bù dǒng, wǒ zhīdào nǐ míngbai.
examples.english: Don't pretend you don't understand; I know you do.

components.note: 片 (slice, plank) — marks flat pieces and wooden boards, as in 牌 sign; 版 is a printing block.
反 (fǎn) hints at the sound: 版 bǎn is close, as in 板 bǎn and 饭 fàn.
木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.

example.hanzi: 这是软件的最新版本。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì ruǎnjiàn de zuìxīn bǎnběn.
example.english: This is the latest version of the software.
example.fact: Linus Torvalds released version 1.0 of the Linux kernel in March 1994, several years after he first announced the project as a hobby operating system in 1991. That kernel now underlies the vast majority of the world's servers, most smartphones through Android, and countless embedded devices. Its version numbering has continued steadily ever since, now well past version 6.

examples.hanzi: 这个游戏有中文版本吗?
examples.pinyin: Zhège yóuxì yǒu Zhōngwén bǎnběn ma?
examples.english: Does this game have a Chinese version?

examples.hanzi: 这本书出了两个版本,内容不太一样。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū chūle liǎng gè bǎnběn, nèiróng bú tài yíyàng.
examples.english: This book has two editions, and the content differs a bit.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔, 等, 算: a hollow pipe.
官 (guān) is a close sound clue for guǎn; 官 also in 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.

example.hanzi: 这条管道输送石油。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo guǎndào shūsòng shíyóu.
example.english: This pipeline transports oil.
example.fact: The Trans-Alaska Pipeline System, completed in 1977, stretches about 1,300 kilometers from the oil fields at Prudhoe Bay on the Arctic coast down to the ice-free port of Valdez. It crosses three mountain ranges and hundreds of rivers and streams along the way. Because much of the ground it crosses is permafrost, long sections of the pipeline are raised above ground on supports to prevent the pipe's heat from melting the frozen soil beneath it.

examples.hanzi: 厨房的水管道堵住了,水流不出去。
examples.pinyin: Chúfáng de shuǐ guǎndào dǔzhù le, shuǐ liú bù chūqù.
examples.english: The kitchen's water pipe is blocked, so the water can't drain.

examples.hanzi: 他通过各种管道了解到这个消息。
examples.pinyin: Tā tōngguò gèzhǒng guǎndào liǎojiě dào zhège xiāoxi.
examples.english: He learned this news through various channels.

components.note: 十 (ten) — a cross: first a single vertical line, later crossed with a horizontal bar. Seen in 十分, 二十, and in 千.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室.
子 (child) — a child in a house: to bear and nurture; characters were later "born" from other characters.
木 (wood) — wooden things: 桌, 板, 桥; 架 is a wooden frame or rack.
加 (jiā) is a near sound match for jià; also in 驾 jià and 嘉 jiā.

example.hanzi: 他脖子上戴着一个十字架。
example.pinyin: Tā bózi shàng dàizhe yí gè shízìjià.
example.english: He wears a cross around his neck.
example.fact: The Red Cross movement was founded in Geneva in 1863 by Swiss businessman Henry Dunant after he witnessed the aftermath of the Battle of Solferino. Its emblem, a red cross on a white background, was chosen simply by reversing the colors of the Swiss flag as a tribute to the country where the organization began. Dunant went on to receive the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.

examples.hanzi: 教堂的屋顶上有一个大十字架。
examples.pinyin: Jiàotáng de wūdǐng shàng yǒu yí gè dà shízìjià.
examples.english: There is a big cross on the church roof.

examples.hanzi: 医院门口的牌子上画着红十字架。
examples.pinyin: Yīyuàn ménkǒu de páizi shàng huàzhe hóng shízìjià.
examples.english: A red cross is painted on the sign at the hospital entrance.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: receiving something by hand.
妾 (qiè) is only a loose sound clue for jiē.
⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔, 等, 算: a hollow pipe.
官 (guān) is a close sound clue for guǎn; 官 also in 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.

example.hanzi: 新经理接管了这个部门。
example.pinyin: Xīn jīnglǐ jiēguǎn le zhège bùmén.
example.english: The new manager took over the department.
example.fact: The 1988 leveraged buyout of RJR Nabisco, in which KKR took over the food and tobacco conglomerate for roughly $25 billion, was the largest corporate takeover of its era. The battle for control, chronicled in the book "Barbarians at the Gate," involved rival bidding groups competing right up until the final vote by the company's board. For years afterward it remained the largest LBO ever completed.

examples.hanzi: 爸爸退休后,我接管了家里的生意。
examples.pinyin: Bàba tuìxiū hòu, wǒ jiēguǎnle jiālǐ de shēngyi.
examples.english: After Dad retired, I took over the family business.

examples.hanzi: 明天开始,由小张接管这个项目。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān kāishǐ, yóu Xiǎo Zhāng jiēguǎn zhège xiàngmù.
examples.english: Starting tomorrow, Xiao Zhang will take over this project.

components.note: 舌 (tongue) — the left part, as in 话 speech. Memory aid: too many wagging tongues create chaos, hence 混乱.
乚 (hook) — the right-hand stroke and dictionary radical. 乱 is simplified from 亂; the stroke does not add meaning.
七 (qī) — seven; as a part it sounds out 切 qiē (cut, with 刀 knife) and 柒 qī.
八 (eight) — originally two strokes pulling apart, meaning divide; that sense is in 分 divide, 公 public and 半 half.
米 (rice) — grain and food, as in 粉 powder, 糕 cake, 精 refined: 糟 is dregs of fermented rice, then spoiled.
曹 (cáo) is a close sound clue for zāo; 曹 also in 遭 zāo and 槽 cáo.

example.hanzi: 他的房间乱七八糟。
example.pinyin: Tā de fángjiān luànqībāzāo.
example.english: His room is in complete disarray.
example.fact: Meteorologist Edward Lorenz stumbled onto the idea now known as the butterfly effect in 1961, while re-running a weather simulation with a slightly rounded-off starting number. The tiny rounding difference produced a completely different forecast within a few simulated days. His finding helped launch chaos theory, showing that some systems are so sensitive to initial conditions that long-term prediction becomes practically impossible.

examples.hanzi: 孩子把玩具扔得乱七八糟。
examples.pinyin: Háizi bǎ wánjù rēng de luànqībāzāo.
examples.english: The child threw the toys all over in a mess.

examples.hanzi: 我的脑子乱七八糟,什么也想不清楚。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de nǎozi luànqībāzāo, shénme yě xiǎng bù qīngchu.
examples.english: My head is a muddle and I can't think clearly about anything.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 衤 is the clothing radical, as in 衣, 裤, 衬; 被 is a quilt, then the passive marker.
皮 (pí) — loose hint — 被 is bèi; 皮 also sounds out 披 pī and 坡 pō.
害 (hài) is a loose sound clue for 割 gē and 辖 xiá; as a word it means to harm, as in 厉害.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查被害人的身份。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá bèihàirén de shēnfèn.
example.english: The police are investigating the victim's identity.
example.fact: Scotland Yard adopted fingerprint identification as an official crime-solving tool in 1901, based on a classification system devised by British official Edward Henry. It replaced the earlier Bertillon system, which relied on detailed body measurements and was far more error-prone. Fingerprint matching quickly became a cornerstone of criminal investigation worldwide and remains in wide use over a century later.

examples.hanzi: 被害人已经被送往医院抢救。
examples.pinyin: Bèihàirén yǐjīng bèi sòngwǎng yīyuàn qiǎngjiù.
examples.english: The victim has been rushed to the hospital for emergency treatment.

examples.hanzi: 被害人向警察描述了当时的情况。
examples.pinyin: Bèihàirén xiàng jǐngchá miáoshùle dāngshí de qíngkuàng.
examples.english: The victim described the situation at the time to the police.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 洒 is sprinkling water.
西 (xī) — loose sound hint (sǎ vs xī); same part in 晒 shài.

example.hanzi: 不小心把水洒在桌子上了。
example.pinyin: Bù xiǎoxīn bǎ shuǐ sǎ zài zhuōzi shàng le.
example.english: I accidentally spilled water on the table.
example.fact: 洒 is used for liquids (洒水, 洒泪), while 撒 (sǎ) is for solids like seeds or salt. 洒脱 and 潇洒 describe a free and easy style. Do not mix it up with 酒 (jiǔ, alcohol).

examples.hanzi: 孩子把牛奶洒在了地上。
examples.pinyin: Háizi bǎ niúnǎi sǎ zài le dìshàng.
examples.english: The child spilled milk on the floor.

examples.hanzi: 早上有人在路上洒水。
examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang yǒu rén zài lù shàng sǎshuǐ.
examples.english: In the morning someone was sprinkling water on the road.

components.note: 缶 (clay jar) — marks pots and jars, as in 罐 jar, 缸 vat; a chipped jar is 缺, lacking.
夬 (guài/jué) is a loose hint for quē; 决 jué and 快 kuài share it.
小 (small) — a 小 with a stroke taken off: not much. 少 also gives sound to 沙 shā, 抄 chāo and 炒 chǎo.

example.hanzi: 这个计划缺少足够的资金。
example.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà quēshǎo zúgòu de zījīn.
example.english: This plan lacks sufficient funding.
example.fact: In 1747, Scottish naval surgeon James Lind ran one of the first controlled clinical trials in medical history, giving groups of scurvy-stricken sailors different remedies to compare. He found that the sailors who ate citrus fruit recovered dramatically faster than the others. Scurvy, it turned out, was caused by a simple lack of vitamin C, though it took the British navy decades to fully adopt citrus rations based on his findings.

examples.hanzi: 我最近睡眠很缺少,总是觉得累。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuìjìn shuìmián hěn quēshǎo, zǒngshì juéde lèi.
examples.english: I've been short on sleep lately and always feel tired.

examples.hanzi: 这道菜缺少一点盐,味道不够好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài quēshǎo yìdiǎn yán, wèidào bú gòu hǎo.
examples.english: This dish lacks a little salt, so it doesn't taste good enough.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood and trees, as in 树, 林, 桌: 校 first meant a wooden frame or restraint.
交 (jiāo) is a close sound clue for xiào; 交 also in 较 jiào and 校 xiào.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国 country, 回 return, 图 map; 园 is a fenced garden.
元 (yuán) sounds exactly like 园; also in 远 yuǎn, 院 yuàn, 完 wán.

example.hanzi: 学生们喜欢在校园里散步。
example.pinyin: Xuéshēngmen xǐhuān zài xiàoyuán lǐ sànbù.
example.english: Students like to take walks around the campus.
example.fact: Teaching is documented at Oxford as far back as 1096, making it the oldest university in the English-speaking world. It grew rapidly after 1167, when English students were banned from studying at the University of Paris and many returned home to study locally instead. Unlike many modern universities, Oxford has no single unified campus; its colleges are scattered as independent institutions throughout the city.

examples.hanzi: 我们的校园里有一个很大的湖。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de xiàoyuán lǐ yǒu yí gè hěn dà de hú.
examples.english: There's a very big lake on our campus.

examples.hanzi: 他周末常常带女儿到校园里骑车。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhōumò chángcháng dài nǚ'ér dào xiàoyuán lǐ qí chē.
examples.english: On weekends he often takes his daughter cycling around the campus.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.
酉 (wine jar) — drink and its rituals, as in 酒 liquor, 醉 drunk; 酬 first meant to toast a guest.
州 (zhōu) is a loose sound clue; it also sounds out 洲 zhōu.

example.hanzi: 他为这份工作要求更高的报酬。
example.pinyin: Tā wèi zhè fèn gōngzuò yāoqiú gèng gāo de bàochou.
example.english: He is asking for higher pay for this job.
example.fact: New Zealand passed one of the world's first national minimum wage laws in 1894, as part of the Industrial Conciliation and Arbitration Act. The law was meant to guarantee workers a baseline income and reduce the labor disputes that had become common in the country. It influenced similar legislation in Australia and, eventually, minimum wage laws adopted across much of the world in the twentieth century.

examples.hanzi: 这份工作的报酬不高,但很有意义。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn gōngzuò de bàochou bù gāo, dàn hěn yǒu yìyì.
examples.english: The pay for this job isn't high, but it's very meaningful.

examples.hanzi: 他帮了我们很多忙,却不要任何报酬。
examples.pinyin: Tā bāngle wǒmen hěn duō máng, què bú yào rènhé bàochou.
examples.english: He helped us a lot but wouldn't accept any payment.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.
青 (qīng) hints at the -ing rhyme; same part in 清 请 情 晴 精. The 争 (contend) half is not a reliable clue.

example.hanzi: 屋子里没有一点动静。
example.pinyin: Wūzi lǐ méiyǒu yìdiǎn dòngjìng.
example.english: There wasn't a sound in the room.
example.fact: Modern seismographs are sensitive enough to detect ground movements smaller than the width of an atom. This extraordinary sensitivity lets scientists register earthquakes from thousands of kilometers away and even pick up faint vibrations from ocean waves, wind, and distant traffic. The technology has advanced enormously since the first practical seismograph was built in the 1870s.

examples.hanzi: 半夜听到楼上有动静,我吓了一跳。
examples.pinyin: Bànyè tīngdào lóushàng yǒu dòngjing, wǒ xiàle yí tiào.
examples.english: I heard a noise upstairs in the middle of the night and was startled.

examples.hanzi: 对方一直没什么动静,不知道在想什么。
examples.pinyin: Duìfāng yìzhí méi shénme dòngjing, bù zhīdào zài xiǎng shénme.
examples.english: The other side has shown no sign of activity and I don't know what they're thinking.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions applied to people: 放, 改, 政; 教 is to teach, traditionally with a rod.
孝 (xiào) is a near sound match for jiào; also in 酵 jiào.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 字: a room under the roof.
至 (zhì, arrive) is a loose sound clue for shì; it fits the meaning: where one arrives inside the house.

example.hanzi: 老师走进了教室。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī zǒu jìn le jiàoshì.
example.english: The teacher walked into the classroom.
example.fact: The University of Al Quaraouiyine in Fez, Morocco, founded in 859 AD, is recognized by UNESCO and the Guinness World Records as the oldest continually operating educational institution in the world. It began as a mosque with attached religious and legal instruction before formally becoming a university. Classes have continued there, with interruptions, for over eleven centuries.

examples.hanzi: 教室里坐满了认真听课的学生。
examples.pinyin: Jiàoshì lǐ zuòmǎnle rènzhēn tīngkè de xuésheng.
examples.english: The classroom was full of students listening attentively.

examples.hanzi: 我的教室在三楼,左边第二间。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jiàoshì zài sān lóu, zuǒbiān dì èr jiān.
examples.english: My classroom is on the third floor, the second room on the left.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: to prove by saying.
正 (zhèng) gives the exact sound; 正 also in 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位.
牛 (ox) — in the traditional reading, a person 亻 dividing up an ox: one piece, hence 件 as a measure word for items.

example.hanzi: 请出示您的证件。
example.pinyin: Qǐng chūshì nín de zhèngjiàn.
example.english: Please show your ID.
example.fact: Standardized passports as we know them largely date to a League of Nations conference in 1920, which recommended a common booklet format for international travel documents. Before that, passports varied wildly in size, format, and the information they contained from country to country. The basic booklet design recommended in 1920 still underlies the ICAO-standardized passports used almost everywhere today.

examples.hanzi: 办理手续时,别忘了带身份证件。
examples.pinyin: Bànlǐ shǒuxù shí, bié wàngle dài shēnfèn zhèngjiàn.
examples.english: Don't forget to bring your ID papers when you handle the formalities.

examples.hanzi: 我的证件放在包里,找不到了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de zhèngjiàn fàng zài bāo lǐ, zhǎo bú dào le.
examples.english: My papers were in my bag and I can't find them.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — oldest form: a person bending over a basin of water to see a reflection; 鉴 jiàn (mirror) adds metal. To look closely, to supervise.
示 (altar, ritual) — 示 (礻 on the left side) marks rites and the sacred, as in 神, 礼, 福; 禁 is taboo, then forbidden.
林 (lín) — near sound — 禁 is jìn; 林 also sounds out 襟 jīn.

example.hanzi: 他因盗窃被监禁三年。
example.pinyin: Tā yīn dàoqiè bèi jiānjìn sān nián.
example.english: He was imprisoned for three years for theft.
example.fact: Alcatraz Island's federal penitentiary operated from 1934 to 1963 in San Francisco Bay, holding notorious inmates such as Al Capone. Officially, no prisoner ever successfully escaped and survived, despite at least fourteen attempts across the prison's history. The fate of three inmates who vanished in a famous 1962 escape attempt, using a raft made of raincoats, has never been conclusively determined.

examples.hanzi: 那个犯人被监禁了十年。
examples.pinyin: Nàge fànrén bèi jiānjìnle shí nián.
examples.english: That criminal was imprisoned for ten years.

examples.hanzi: 他不想被监禁在这个小房间里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng bèi jiānjìn zài zhège xiǎo fángjiān lǐ.
examples.english: He doesn't want to be confined in this small room.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 灬 is fire at the bottom, as in 点, 照, 熟; 热 is heat.
灬 (fire) — the four-dot form of 火, as in 热 hot, 点 point, 煮 cook; 烈 is blazing, then intense.
列 (liè) gives the sound exactly: 烈 liè, also in 裂 liè (split).

example.hanzi: 观众对表演报以热烈的掌声。
example.pinyin: Guānzhòng duì biǎoyǎn bào yǐ rèliè de zhǎngshēng.
example.english: The audience gave the performance enthusiastic applause.
example.fact: The 1883 eruption of the volcano Krakatoa in Indonesia produced what is often called the loudest sound in recorded history. It was clearly heard by observers roughly 3,000 miles away on the island of Rodrigues, near Mauritius, who described it as distant cannon fire. The pressure wave from the blast circled the entire globe multiple times, registering on barometers worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 大家热烈欢迎新同学的到来。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā rèliè huānyíng xīn tóngxué de dàolái.
examples.english: Everyone warmly welcomed the arrival of the new classmate.

examples.hanzi: 晚会上的气氛非常热烈。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnhuì shàng de qìfēn fēicháng rèliè.
examples.english: The atmosphere at the evening party was very lively.

components.note: 田 (field) — the bottom part. 备 is simplified from 備; the dictionary story is a trip to the 田 field to prepare for harvest. Treat it as a memory aid.
夂 (going down, slow step) — the top. Memory aid: heading 夂 to the field 田 to get ready — 准备, 设备.

example.hanzi: 明天要考试，我今晚要准备一下。
example.pinyin: Míngtiān yào kǎoshì, wǒ jīnwǎn yào zhǔnbèi yíxià.
example.english: There is an exam tomorrow, so I need to prepare tonight.
example.fact: 备 is to prepare: 准备, 预备, 备课 (to prepare a lesson), 设备 (equipment), 备份 (backup), 备注 (a note field on a form). It is a simplified form of 備.

examples.hanzi: 出门前，我们要先准备好雨伞。
examples.pinyin: Chūmén qián, wǒmen yào xiān zhǔnbèi hǎo yǔsǎn.
examples.english: Before going out, we need to get our umbrellas ready.

examples.hanzi: 这家宾馆设备很齐全。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā bīnguǎn shèbèi hěn qíquán.
examples.english: This hotel is fully equipped.

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — marks birds, as in 难, 谁 (loan uses), 集; 雅 first named a crow, now borrowed for 'elegant'.
牙 (yá) hints at the sound: 雅 yǎ is close to 鸦 yā and 呀 ya.

example.hanzi: 他的举止很文雅。
example.pinyin: Tā de jǔzhǐ hěn wényǎ.
example.english: His manners are very refined.
example.fact: 雅 means elegant: 文雅, 优雅, 高雅, 雅致 (tasteful). The elegant sense is a loan; the character first named a bird. 雅思 is how IELTS is written in Chinese, and 雅座 means a private booth in a restaurant.

examples.hanzi: 她说话的声音很文雅。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà de shēngyīn hěn wényǎ.
examples.english: The way she speaks is very refined.

examples.hanzi: 这间茶室布置得很雅致。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiān cháshì bùzhì de hěn yǎzhì.
examples.english: This tea room is decorated in a very tasteful way.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
言 (speech) — 言 is the traditional full form of the 讠 radical for speech and language: 说, 话, 语, 请.

example.hanzi: 代表们轮流上台发言。
example.pinyin: Dàibiǎomen lúnliú shàngtái fāyán.
example.english: The delegates took turns going on stage to speak.
example.fact: Abraham Lincoln's Gettysburg Address, delivered in 1863, lasted only about two minutes and roughly 270 words. Contemporary newspaper accounts noted that the crowd barely had time to react before Lincoln had already finished and sat down. Despite its brevity, it went on to become one of the most quoted speeches in American history.

examples.hanzi: 会议上,请大家积极发言。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì shàng, qǐng dàjiā jījí fāyán.
examples.english: At the meeting, please all speak up actively.

examples.hanzi: 他在课堂上很少发言,总是静静地听。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài kètáng shàng hěn shǎo fāyán, zǒngshì jìngjìng de tīng.
examples.english: He rarely speaks in class and always listens quietly.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 这不是我的书。
example.pinyin: Zhè bùshì wǒ de shū.
example.english: This is not my book.
example.fact: Pluto is officially not a planet since 2006, when the International Astronomical Union adopted a formal definition of 'planet' that requires an object to have cleared its orbital neighborhood of other debris. Pluto shares its orbit with many other icy bodies in the Kuiper Belt, so it was reclassified as a 'dwarf planet.' The decision remains controversial among some astronomers even decades later.

examples.hanzi: 我不是学生,我已经工作了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú shì xuésheng, wǒ yǐjīng gōngzuò le.
examples.english: I'm not a student; I'm already working.

examples.hanzi: 你不是说今天要来吗?怎么还没到?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bú shì shuō jīntiān yào lái ma? Zěnme hái méi dào?
examples.english: Didn't you say you were coming today? Why haven't you arrived yet?

components.note: 后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).
阝 on the left is 阜 (mound) — as in 险, 阳, 阴: a walled yard.
完 (wán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; also in 玩 wán.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在后院玩耍。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài hòuyuàn wánshuǎ.
example.english: The children are playing in the backyard.
example.fact: In 1954, a meteorite crashed through the roof of Ann Hodges's home in Sylacauga, Alabama, bounced off a radio, and struck her while she napped on the couch. It remains one of the only confirmed cases in recorded history of a person being directly hit by a meteorite. Hodges suffered a large bruise but survived, and the rock is now known as the Hodges Meteorite.

examples.hanzi: 我家后院种了几棵苹果树。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā hòuyuàn zhòngle jǐ kē píngguǒ shù.
examples.english: We planted a few apple trees in our backyard.

examples.hanzi: 周末我们在后院烤肉吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen zài hòuyuàn kǎoròu chī.
examples.english: On weekends we have a barbecue in the backyard.

components.note: 兽 (simplified 獸) — the old form paired a hunted animal with a dog 犬; it means beast, as in 野兽 and 怪兽.

example.hanzi: 森林里有很多野兽。
example.pinyin: Sēnlín lǐ yǒu hěn duō yěshòu.
example.english: There are many wild beasts in the forest.
example.fact: 兽 refers to four-legged beasts: 野兽 (wild animal), 怪兽 (monster), 兽医 (veterinarian). 禽兽 (birds and beasts) is an insult for a brutal person, and 衣冠禽兽 describes a well-dressed scoundrel.

examples.hanzi: 动物园里有一只凶猛的野兽。
examples.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ yǒu yì zhī xiōngměng de yěshòu.
examples.english: There is a fierce beast in the zoo.

examples.hanzi: 他想当一名兽医，照顾小动物。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng dāng yì míng shòuyī, zhàogù xiǎo dòngwù.
examples.english: He wants to be a vet and take care of small animals.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说, 话, 请; 谎 is a spoken lie.
荒 (huāng) sounds the same as 谎 huǎng except for tone; also 慌 huāng.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.

example.hanzi: 他为自己编造了一个谎话。
example.pinyin: Tā wèi zìjǐ biānzào le yí gè huǎnghuà.
example.english: He made up a lie for himself.
example.fact: The modern polygraph, popularly known as the lie detector, was developed in the early 1920s by John Larson, a police officer and physiologist in California. It measures changes in heart rate, blood pressure, and skin conductivity that can accompany stress. Despite its long use in interrogations, courts in many countries have never fully accepted polygraph results as reliable scientific evidence.

examples.hanzi: 小孩说谎话时,眼睛不敢看人。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎohái shuō huǎnghuà shí, yǎnjing bù gǎn kàn rén.
examples.english: When children tell lies, they don't dare look people in the eye.

examples.hanzi: 他说的都是谎话,别相信他。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō de dōu shì huǎnghuà, bié xiāngxìn tā.
examples.english: Everything he says is a lie, so don't believe him.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and discussion: 说, 议, 谈; 论 is debate and theory.
仑 (lún) gives the sound; same part in 轮 lún and 伦 lún.
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 无论是晴天还是雨天,他都坚持跑步。
example.pinyin: Wúlùnshì qíngtiān háishi yǔtiān, tā dōu jiānchí pǎobù.
example.english: Whether it is sunny or rainy, he keeps running.
example.fact: The Mount Washington Observatory in New Hampshire recorded a wind gust of 372 kilometers per hour in April 1934, at the time the fastest wind speed ever directly measured by a person at Earth's surface. The mountain's summit sits at the intersection of several major storm tracks, making it one of the most consistently extreme weather locations in the world. Its record stood for six decades before being surpassed by a 1996 measurement during a tropical cyclone in Australia.

examples.hanzi: 无论是大人还是小孩,都喜欢这部动画片。
examples.pinyin: Wúlùn shì dàrén háishi xiǎohái, dōu xǐhuan zhè bù dònghuàpiàn.
examples.english: Whether adults or children, everyone likes this cartoon.

examples.hanzi: 无论是现在还是将来,我都会支持你。
examples.pinyin: Wúlùn shì xiànzài háishi jiānglái, wǒ dōu huì zhīchí nǐ.
examples.english: Whether now or in the future, I will support you.

meanings: to throw sb to the ground

components.note: 扌 (hand) — to throw down by hand; also in 打 hit, 扔 throw.
率 (shuài) gives the same syllable with a different tone.
亻 (person) — a person falling over; marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做.
到 (dào) gives the sound: 倒 is dǎo (fall) or dào (upside down).

example.hanzi: 老人在冰面上摔倒了。
example.pinyin: Lǎorén zài bīngmiàn shàng shuāidǎo le.
example.english: The elderly man fell on the icy surface.
example.fact: Falls are a leading cause of accidental injury and death among people over 65 in many countries, according to public health researchers. Part of the danger comes from simple physics: the friction coefficient of ice can drop below 0.05, far lower than the 0.5 to 0.8 typical of dry pavement, making it far easier to lose one's footing suddenly and without warning.

examples.hanzi: 小心点,别在湿地板上摔倒了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn diǎn, bié zài shī dìbǎn shàng shuāidǎo le.
examples.english: Be careful not to slip and fall on the wet floor.

examples.hanzi: 他骑车时摔倒了,膝盖受了伤。
examples.pinyin: Tā qí chē shí shuāidǎo le, xīgài shòule shāng.
examples.english: He fell off his bike and hurt his knee.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话; 辩 puts two 辛 (offenders) with words between them, an argument.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and discussion: 说, 议, 谈; 论 is debate and theory.
仑 (lún) gives the sound; same part in 轮 lún and 伦 lún.

example.hanzi: 两位候选人展开了激烈的辩论。
example.pinyin: Liǎng wèi hòuxuǎnrén zhǎnkāi le jīliè de biànlùn.
example.english: The two candidates engaged in a heated debate.
example.fact: The first televised U.S. presidential debate took place on September 26, 1960, between John F. Kennedy and Richard Nixon. An estimated 70 million viewers tuned in, and many historians credit Kennedy's composed appearance on camera, compared with a sweating, underslept Nixon, with helping tip the close election in his favor. The debate marked a turning point in how television would shape political campaigns.

examples.hanzi: 同学们在课上辩论环保问题。
examples.pinyin: Tóngxuémen zài kè shàng biànlùn huánbǎo wèntí.
examples.english: The students debated environmental issues in class.

examples.hanzi: 我们学校每年都举办辩论比赛。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xuéxiào měi nián dōu jǔbàn biànlùn bǐsài.
examples.english: Our school holds a debate competition every year.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people, as in 你, 他, 做; 仇 is an enemy, a person you hate.
九 (jiǔ) is only a loose sound hint for chóu.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid; 恨 is hatred in the heart.
艮 (gèn) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 很 hěn, 根 gēn and 跟 gēn.

example.hanzi: 这场战争源于多年的仇恨。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng zhànzhēng yuányú duōnián de chóuhèn.
example.english: This war stemmed from years of hatred.
example.fact: A 2008 study by researchers at University College London used brain scans to identify a distinct neural network activated when people view images of someone they hate. The pattern overlapped with regions of the brain, including the putamen and insula, that are also involved in generating aggressive behavior. The findings suggested that hatred, unlike simple anger, engages a somewhat unique combination of brain circuits.

examples.hanzi: 他心里充满了对敌人的仇恨。
examples.pinyin: Tā xīnlǐ chōngmǎnle duì dírén de chóuhèn.
examples.english: His heart was filled with hatred for the enemy.

examples.hanzi: 仇恨只会带来更多的痛苦。
examples.pinyin: Chóuhèn zhǐ huì dàilái gèng duō de tòngkǔ.
examples.english: Hatred only brings more pain.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 代 is one person replacing another, then a generation.
弋 (yì) is only a loose hint; 代 itself sounds out 袋 dài and 贷 dài.
石 (stone) — stones and minerals: 破, 研, 砖; 码 first meant stone weights, then numbers.
马 (mǎ) sounds exactly like 码; also in 吗, 骂 mà, 妈 mā.

example.hanzi: 程序员正在检查这段代码。
example.pinyin: Chéngxùyuán zhèngzài jiǎnchá zhè duàn dàimǎ.
example.english: The programmer is checking this piece of code.
example.fact: The term 'bug' for a technical defect gained wide popularity in computing after a moth was found jammed in a relay of the Harvard Mark II computer in 1947, causing a malfunction. Engineers taped the moth into the logbook with the note 'first actual case of bug being found.' The word itself predates that incident by decades, but the anecdote helped cement it permanently into engineering culture.

examples.hanzi: 你能帮我看看这段代码哪里错了吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng bāng wǒ kànkan zhè duàn dàimǎ nǎlǐ cuò le ma?
examples.english: Can you help me see what's wrong with this piece of code?

examples.hanzi: 他每天晚上都写代码到很晚。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān wǎnshang dōu xiě dàimǎ dào hěn wǎn.
examples.english: He writes code late into the night every day.

components.note: 能 (can) — originally a picture of a bear, a strong animal (熊 xióng adds fire 灬); "strong, able" gave "can".
氵 (water) — marks water and rivers, as in 河, 海; 源 is the spring where water starts.
原 (yuán) gives the sound exactly: 源 yuán, also in 愿 yuàn.

example.hanzi: 太阳能是一种清洁的能源。
example.pinyin: Tàiyángnéng shì yì zhǒng qīngjié de néngyuán.
example.english: Solar power is a clean source of energy.
example.fact: The sun converts roughly 4 million tons of its own mass into energy every single second through nuclear fusion, radiating about 3.8 x 10^26 watts in all directions. Earth intercepts only a tiny fraction of that output, yet it is still far more energy than humanity currently uses in a year. The conversion follows Einstein's famous relation E = mc², linking mass directly to energy.

examples.hanzi: 我们要节约能源,少开空调。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào jiéyuē néngyuán, shǎo kāi kōngtiáo.
examples.english: We should save energy and use the air conditioning less.

examples.hanzi: 这个国家的能源主要来自水力。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de néngyuán zhǔyào láizì shuǐlì.
examples.english: This country's energy mainly comes from hydropower.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 使 is sending someone to do something.
吏 (lì, official) gives the meaning, and shares its ancestor 史 (shǐ), the exact sound of 使.

example.hanzi: 他被任命为驻美大使。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi rènmìng wéi zhù Měi dàshǐ.
example.english: He was appointed ambassador to the United States.
example.fact: Permanent resident embassies, rather than temporary diplomatic missions, are usually traced to the Italian Renaissance city-states. Milan is credited with sending one of the first known permanent ambassadors, to the court of Genoa around 1455. The practice spread across Europe over the following century, eventually becoming the standard model for diplomacy still used by nations today.

examples.hanzi: 大使在欢迎晚宴上发表了讲话。
examples.pinyin: Dàshǐ zài huānyíng wǎnyàn shàng fābiǎole jiǎnghuà.
examples.english: The ambassador gave a speech at the welcome dinner.

examples.hanzi: 中国驻法国大使今天见了记者。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó zhù Fǎguó dàshǐ jīntiān jiànle jìzhě.
examples.english: The Chinese ambassador to France met reporters today.

components.note: 页 (head) — 页 is the head, as in 题, 顶, 颜; 领 is the neck and then to lead.
令 (lìng) — near sound — 领 is lǐng; 令 also sounds out 龄 líng and 铃 líng.
羊 (yáng) hints at the sound: 养 yǎng is close, as in 样 yàng and 洋 yáng; the old form 養 added 食 food.

example.hanzi: 他们决定领养一个孩子。
example.pinyin: Tāmen juédìng lǐngyǎng yí gè háizi.
example.english: They decided to adopt a child.
example.fact: Researchers studying emperor penguin colonies in Antarctica have documented cases of adult penguins 'adopting' chicks that are not biologically their own, typically after losing their own egg or chick earlier in the season. This behavior can sometimes turn competitive, with several adults attempting to claim the same stray chick at once. It remains one of the more striking examples of parental instinct persisting even without a genetic link.

examples.hanzi: 我想从动物收容所领养一只猫。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng cóng dòngwù shōuróngsuǒ lǐngyǎng yì zhī māo.
examples.english: I'd like to adopt a cat from the animal shelter.

examples.hanzi: 这对夫妻领养了一个小女孩。
examples.pinyin: Zhè duì fūqī lǐngyǎngle yí gè xiǎo nǚhái.
examples.english: This couple adopted a little girl.

components.note: 取 (qǔ, take) is a loose sound clue for jù; the part below shows people gathered together.
隹 (short-tailed bird) — birds: 难, 雀, 雄; 集 is birds 隹 gathered on a tree 木: to gather.

example.hanzi: 人群在广场上聚集。
example.pinyin: Rénqún zài guǎngchǎng shàng jùjí.
example.english: A crowd gathered in the square.
example.fact: Globular star clusters such as Omega Centauri can contain up to 10 million stars, all gravitationally bound together within a region only about 150 light-years across. That packs an enormous stellar population into a comparatively tiny volume of space. Astronomers believe some globular clusters may even be the stripped-down cores of small galaxies that were absorbed by larger ones long ago.

examples.hanzi: 下课后,同学们聚集在操场上。
examples.pinyin: Xiàkè hòu, tóngxuémen jùjí zài cāochǎng shàng.
examples.english: After class, the students gathered on the playground.

examples.hanzi: 很多鸟聚集在湖边找东西吃。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō niǎo jùjí zài húbiān zhǎo dōngxi chī.
examples.english: Many birds gather by the lake to look for food.

meanings: Brooklyn, borough of New York City

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — 巾 is a cloth radical, as in 帽 hat, 带 belt; 布 is cloth, and by extension to spread or announce, as in 宣布.
鱼 (fish) — the old 魯 had fish on top; the meaning 'foolish, rash' is later and not about fish. 鲁 is mostly the state and surname Lu.
日 (sun) — at the bottom (from older 白). Memory aid: a fish gaping in the sun is dazed — hence foolish, rash.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.
木 (tree) — two trees side by side make a grove or forest; compare 森 with three.

example.hanzi: 他们去布鲁克林大桥散步。
example.pinyin: Tāmen qù Bùlǔkèlín Dàqiáo sànbù.
example.english: They went for a walk on the Brooklyn Bridge.
example.fact: The Brooklyn Bridge opened in 1883 after fourteen years of construction, connecting Manhattan and Brooklyn across the East River. At the time it opened, its main span of 1,595 feet made it the longest suspension bridge in the world. Its chief engineer, John Roebling, died from an infection following an injury sustained while surveying the site, and his son Washington Roebling oversaw the bridge's completion.

examples.hanzi: 我们周末去布鲁克林看了一场球赛。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò qù Bùlǔkèlín kànle yì chǎng qiúsài.
examples.english: We went to Brooklyn at the weekend to watch a ball game.

examples.hanzi: 他住在纽约的布鲁克林,离地铁站很近。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhù zài Niǔyuē de Bùlǔkèlín, lí dìtiězhàn hěn jìn.
examples.english: He lives in Brooklyn, New York, very close to a subway station.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — body-part radical, as in 肝 liver, 肺 lung, 脑 brain.
田 here is not a field but an old picture of a stomach holding food.
口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.

example.hanzi: 生病让他失去了胃口。
example.pinyin: Shēngbìng ràng tā shīqù le wèikǒu.
example.english: Being sick made him lose his appetite.
example.fact: The hormone ghrelin, discovered in 1999, is produced mainly by cells lining the stomach and is often called the 'hunger hormone.' Its levels rise sharply before a meal and drop again shortly after eating, signaling to the brain when the body needs fuel. Researchers have since found that ghrelin also affects mood, memory, and sleep, well beyond its original role in appetite.

examples.hanzi: 我今天胃口很好,吃了三碗饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān wèikǒu hěn hǎo, chīle sān wǎn fàn.
examples.english: I have a good appetite today and ate three bowls of rice.

examples.hanzi: 这道菜很对我的胃口。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài hěn duì wǒ de wèikǒu.
examples.english: This dish is just to my taste.

components.note: 周 (zhōu) also lends its sound to 调 diào/tiáo, 稠 chóu, 绸 chóu and 凋 diāo.
二 (two) — two parallel strokes: the next step after 一 and before 三.

example.hanzi: 会议将在下周二举行。
example.pinyin: Huìyì jiāng zài xià zhōu'èr jǔxíng.
example.english: The meeting will be held next Tuesday.
example.fact: October 29, 1929, is remembered as 'Black Tuesday,' the day the New York Stock Exchange suffered its most devastating crash of the era. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost about 12 percent of its value in a single trading session as panicked investors rushed to sell. The crash is widely seen as the event that triggered the decade-long Great Depression that followed.

examples.hanzi: 周二下午我有空,我们见面吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhōu'èr xiàwǔ wǒ yǒu kòng, wǒmen jiànmiàn ba.
examples.english: I'm free on Tuesday afternoon, so let's meet.

examples.hanzi: 我每周二晚上都去游泳。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi zhōu'èr wǎnshang dōu qù yóuyǒng.
examples.english: I go swimming every Tuesday evening.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 值 is worth.
直 (zhí) sounds exactly like 值; also 植 zhí and 置 zhì.
钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 铁, 银, 钟; early money was metal coins.
戋 (jiān) — near sound — 钱 is qián; 戋 also sounds out 浅 qiǎn and 线 xiàn, and means small or thin.

example.hanzi: 这块古董非常值钱。
example.pinyin: Zhè kuài gǔdǒng fēicháng zhíqián.
example.english: This antique is extremely valuable.
example.fact: In 2017, a small Northern Song-dynasty Ru ware brush washer, barely larger than a teacup, sold at auction in Hong Kong for over 294 million Hong Kong dollars, roughly 37 million US dollars at the time. The sale set a record for Chinese ceramics, driven partly by the extreme rarity of surviving Ru ware, of which fewer than 100 complete pieces are known to exist worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 这些旧邮票其实很值钱。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē jiù yóupiào qíshí hěn zhíqián.
examples.english: These old stamps are actually worth a lot.

examples.hanzi: 你包里有什么值钱的东西吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bāo lǐ yǒu shénme zhíqián de dōngxi ma?
examples.english: Do you have anything valuable in your bag?

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海, 汤; 流 is flowing water.
㐬 (liú) — same sound — 流 is liú; 㐬 also sounds out 琉 liú and 硫 liú.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: to drive away, set free.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fàng; 方 also in 房 fáng and 访 fǎng.

example.hanzi: 那位诗人被流放到边疆。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi shīrén bèi liúfàng dào biānjiāng.
example.english: That poet was exiled to the frontier.
example.fact: Napoleon Bonaparte was first exiled to the small Mediterranean island of Elba in 1814 after his abdication, only to escape within a year and briefly return to power. Following his final defeat at Waterloo in 1815, he was exiled a second time, this time to the remote South Atlantic island of Saint Helena, where he lived under British guard until his death in 1821.

examples.hanzi: 古时候,犯了罪的人常被流放到很远的地方。
examples.pinyin: Gǔ shíhou, fànle zuì de rén cháng bèi liúfàng dào hěn yuǎn de dìfang.
examples.english: In ancient times, criminals were often exiled to faraway places.

examples.hanzi: 他在国外流放了十几年,才回到家乡。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài guówài liúfàngle shí jǐ nián, cái huídào jiāxiāng.
examples.english: He lived in exile abroad for more than ten years before returning home.

components.note: 著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.
心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 思, 感, 急: to think of someone.
相 (xiāng) is a close sound clue for xiǎng; 相 also in 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.

example.hanzi: 父母总是为孩子着想。
example.pinyin: Fùmǔ zǒngshì wèi háizi zhuóxiǎng.
example.english: Parents always think of their children.
example.fact: The 'trolley problem,' a thought experiment introduced by philosopher Philippa Foot in 1967 and later expanded by Judith Jarvis Thomson, asks whether it is right to divert a runaway trolley to kill one person instead of five. It has since become a standard tool in psychology and neuroscience for studying how people weigh the interests of others when making difficult moral decisions. Variations of the problem are still used in research on self-driving car ethics today.

examples.hanzi: 我这样说,都是为你着想。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhèyàng shuō, dōu shì wèi nǐ zhuóxiǎng.
examples.english: I'm saying this for your own good.

examples.hanzi: 做事要多为别人着想。
examples.pinyin: Zuòshì yào duō wèi biéren zhuóxiǎng.
examples.english: When you do things, think more about others.

components.note: 亡 (die, lose) — 丧 (simplified 喪) once showed crying 哭 over the dead 亡: mourning, then loss and dejection (沮丧).
夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.

example.hanzi: 事故后,他丧失了部分记忆。
example.pinyin: Shìgù hòu, tā sàngshī le bùfen jìyì.
example.english: After the accident, he lost part of his memory.
example.fact: The patient known in scientific literature as H.M., Henry Molaison, lost the ability to form new long-term memories after undergoing experimental brain surgery in 1953 to treat severe epilepsy. Researchers studied him for decades afterward, and his case became one of the most influential in the history of memory research, helping establish that different brain regions handle different types of memory.

examples.hanzi: 他因为生病丧失了工作能力。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi shēngbìng sàngshīle gōngzuò nénglì.
examples.english: He lost his ability to work because of illness.

examples.hanzi: 遇到困难,不要丧失信心。
examples.pinyin: Yùdào kùnnan, bú yào sàngshī xìnxīn.
examples.english: When you face difficulties, don't lose confidence.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — weather radical, as in 雷 thunder, 雾 fog; snow is frozen rain.
艹 (grass) — plants; 茄 is the eggplant, as in 花 flower, 草 grass.
加 (jiā) gives the sound in 雪茄 xuě jiā; it also sounds out 架 jià and 嘉 jiā.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢在晚饭后抽雪茄。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuān zài wǎnfàn hòu chōu xuějiā.
example.english: He likes to smoke a cigar after dinner.
example.fact: Cuba's Pinar del Río province, particularly its Vuelta Abajo region, is widely regarded by tobacco experts as producing some of the finest cigar tobacco in the world. Its reddish clay soil, high humidity, and specific microclimate are considered difficult to replicate elsewhere. The region has supplied leaf for Cuban cigars for well over a century.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷以前每天抽一根雪茄。
examples.pinyin: Yéye yǐqián měitiān chōu yì gēn xuějiā.
examples.english: Grandpa used to smoke a cigar every day.

examples.hanzi: 这盒雪茄是朋友从古巴带来的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè hé xuějiā shì péngyou cóng Gǔbā dàilái de.
examples.english: This box of cigars was brought from Cuba by a friend.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
衣 (clothes) — a picture of a coat with a collar and sleeves. As a radical it is 衤 on the left: 裤 trousers, 衬 shirt, 被 quilt.

example.hanzi: 她穿了一件红色的上衣。
example.pinyin: Tā chuān le yí jiàn hóngsè de shàngyī.
example.english: She wore a red jacket.
example.fact: Gideon Sundback patented an improved version of the modern zipper in 1913, but it took another one to two decades before manufacturers widely adopted it for clothing such as jackets. Early marketing struggled because the zipper was seen mainly as a novelty for boots and tobacco pouches. It was only in the 1930s, after a push from the fashion industry, that zippers became a standard fastener on everyday garments.

examples.hanzi: 今天有点冷,你多穿一件上衣吧。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān yǒudiǎn lěng, nǐ duō chuān yí jiàn shàngyī ba.
examples.english: It's a bit cold today, so wear an extra top.

examples.hanzi: 这套衣服的上衣太大了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tào yīfu de shàngyī tài dà le.
examples.english: The top of this outfit is too big.

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 情, 快, 怕; 性 is the inner nature of a thing.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint; also in 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 这部电影深刻地探讨了人性。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng shēnkè de tàntǎo le rénxìng.
example.english: This film explores human nature deeply.
example.fact: The Stanford Prison Experiment, run by psychologist Philip Zimbardo in 1971, assigned college students to act as guards or prisoners in a simulated jail and observed how quickly ordinary people adopted abusive or submissive roles. The study was cut short after only six days due to the severity of the behavior it provoked. Decades later, historians and psychologists have raised serious questions about its methodology, but it remains widely cited in discussions of situational influence on behavior.

examples.hanzi: 人性有善的一面,也有恶的一面。
examples.pinyin: Rénxìng yǒu shàn de yímiàn, yě yǒu è de yímiàn.
examples.english: Human nature has a good side and a bad side.

examples.hanzi: 这样的管理方式太不人性了。
examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng de guǎnlǐ fāngshì tài bù rénxìng le.
examples.english: This way of managing is far too inhumane.

components.note: 尸 (body/roof) — the top-left cover, as in 层 and 局. In 展 it works like a cover over cloth that is spread out; memory aid, shape is partly simplified.
衣 (clothing) — a bit of this sits inside 展. Dictionary story: laying out clothes to display them, hence 'unfold, exhibit' in 展示.

example.hanzi: 周末我们去看艺术展。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù kàn yìshù zhǎn.
example.english: This weekend we are going to see an art exhibition.
example.fact: 展 means to spread out: 展开 (unfold), 展示 (display), 发展 (develop), 进展 (progress), 展望 (outlook). On its own it often means an exhibition: 画展 (art show), 车展 (auto show).

examples.hanzi: 美术馆正在举办一个新的画展。
examples.pinyin: Měishùguǎn zhèngzài jǔbàn yí ge xīn de huàzhǎn.
examples.english: The art museum is holding a new painting exhibition.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市的经济发展得很快。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì de jīngjì fāzhǎn de hěn kuài.
examples.english: The economy of this city is developing very fast.

components.note: 米 (rice, grain) — coarse grain, hence rough; also in 粉 powder, 粮 grain.
且 (qiě) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 租 zū and 阻 zǔ.
鱼 (fish) — the old 魯 had fish on top; the meaning 'foolish, rash' is later and not about fish. 鲁 is mostly the state and surname Lu.
日 (sun) — at the bottom (from older 白). Memory aid: a fish gaping in the sun is dazed — hence foolish, rash.

example.hanzi: 他对服务员的态度很粗鲁。
example.pinyin: Tā duì fúwùyuán de tàidù hěn cūlǔ.
example.english: His attitude toward the waiter was very rude.
example.fact: At the court of Louis XIV in seventeenth-century Versailles, strict rules of conduct were literally posted on small placards called 'etiquettes,' the origin of the modern word 'etiquette.' Nobles who violated the posted rules risked real social consequences, including loss of royal favor. The system reflected just how tightly regulated courtly behavior had become under the French monarchy.

examples.hanzi: 你说话别这么粗鲁,要有礼貌。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shuōhuà bié zhème cūlǔ, yào yǒu lǐmào.
examples.english: Don't speak so rudely; be polite.

examples.hanzi: 那个司机的动作很粗鲁,吓到了乘客。
examples.pinyin: Nàge sījī de dòngzuò hěn cūlǔ, xiàdàole chéngkè.
examples.english: That driver's movements were rough and frightened the passengers.
